item.title: Google Launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen for Search and AI Workflows
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends, The Verge, Ars Technica, TechCrunch Original headline: Google Launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen, Enhancing Search and AI Workflows
Google has launched Gemini 4 Hydrogen, its primary AI model for everyday agentic workflows, replacing the Gemini 3.8 Flash model. Available in Gemini app, Google Search, and AI Studio, Hydrogen offers 2.5x faster task completion and 5x fewer fabricated claims than Flash 3.8. In enterprise data analysis, it achieves 2.8x speed improvements and 23% lower token usage. The model supports four thinking levels, including a new xhigh mode for enhanced performance. Robby Stein, VP of Google Search, called it 'the biggest model upgrade to Search yet,' emphasizing its role in AI Overviews for complex queries. Hydrogen improves search results with relevant links, visual responses, and structured data, while enhancing language understanding and typo tolerance. Developers can access it via Gemini API, Android Studio, and AI Studio. Performance benchmarks show Hydrogen outperforms OpenAI’s GPT-6.1 Terra and Anthropic’s Claude Sonnet 5.5 in knowledge and multimodal tasks, though it lags slightly in science/math benchmarks. It matches Gemini 4 Argon in some cases, scoring 54 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index in xhigh mode. Safety improvements reduce AI overreach by 81%, and integration with Gmail and Google Drive enables context-based task execution. The model marks a key step in Google’s AI strategy, balancing speed and intelligence for consumer and enterprise use.
item.source: Digital Trends, The Verge, Ars Technica, TechCrunch

item.title: United Airlines restricts AI agents from booking flights over security concerns
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: United Airlines blocks AI agents from booking flights, citing cybersecurity risks
United Airlines will restrict AI agents from booking flights and managing reservations, citing cybersecurity risks and potential violations of federal regulations. The airline warns that sharing account credentials with third-party AI assistants could expose sensitive data, leading to unintended purchases or account changes. It also highlights risks of bypassing rules requiring human verification for flight check-ins. United is updating booking policies and collaborating with travel agencies to block unauthorized AI access. This follows similar actions by banks like Bank of America, which warned against password sharing with AI assistants. The move aims to differentiate real customers from automated systems and prevent security breaches. United’s statement emphasizes that AI agents may not comply with aviation regulations, such as confirming baggage compliance with security protocols.

item.title: Xbox Insiders Test New Backgrounds and Guide Menu Customizations
item.description:
Source: The Verge Original headline: Xbox owners are getting more customizations for backgrounds and the Guide menu
Microsoft is testing new customization options for Xbox Insiders, including rotating backgrounds, improved digital game organization, and Guide menu positioning. Xbox Insiders can now save favorite dynamic backgrounds and shuffle through them automatically, with options to change backgrounds hourly, daily, or weekly. The feature allows users to set backgrounds to change each time they sign in. Digital game licenses from disc-based titles will appear in a separate library category, with an option to hide the digital license icon on game tiles. Insiders can also choose to place the Guide menu on the left or right side of the screen. Eden Marie, principal software engineering lead at Xbox, noted that Alpha Skip-Ahead members will test these features first, with broader rollout planned for more users over time.

item.title: Microsoft Fixes Outlook Security Flaw, Urges Updates
item.description:
Source: PCWorld Original headline: Microsoft just patched a serious Outlook flaw. Time to update!
Microsoft has patched a security flaw in Outlook designated CVE-2026-124194. The vulnerability allows attackers to trick users into opening tampered message files, potentially enabling unauthorized server connections without security warnings. This risks leaking authentication credentials and allows impersonation. Microsoft classifies the issue as moderately severe but confirms active exploitation. Affected products include Microsoft 365 for business and Office LTSC 2021/2024. The flaw is part of 1,093 addressed in November updates, with 63 labeled critical. CISA added it to its list of actively exploited vulnerabilities. Updates released November 10th are available via Office settings or IT departments for business users. Users are urged to install patches immediately.

item.title: Binance Replaces $6.3 Billion in Stolen Crypto
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: Binance Says It Has Replaced All $6.3 Billion in Crypto Stolen in Record-Breaking Heist
Binance announced it has fully reimbursed $6.34 billion in cryptocurrency stolen during a October 29 hack. The exchange used funds from its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU), futures insurance, and corporate treasury to cover losses. Binance plans to replenish SAFU to $1 billion and released a new Proof of Reserves snapshot to allow user verification of holdings. Withdrawals are being restored in phases. The attack, attributed to North Korean group TraderTraitor, involved stealing assets across 10 blockchains within 20 minutes. TRM Labs and the FBI linked the breach to North Korea, with nearly $3 billion intercepted. Hackers moved remaining funds through thousands of wallets and created memecoins to launder $430,000. Binance identified multiple breach points and is enhancing security measures. The company did not comment on further inquiries.

item.title: Astronomers Identify Source of 8-Minute Radio Signal
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: A Mysterious Radio Signal Repeats Every 8 Minutes. Astronomers Finally Know What’s Behind It
Astronomers have identified the source of a mysterious radio signal repeating every 8 minutes. Detected by the Murchison Widefield Array in late 2024, the signal from GPM J071507−114153 was classified as a long-period transient. A study published in Nature Astronomy links the signal to a binary star system containing a white dwarf and a G-type star like our Sun. This marks the first detection of radio pulses from a white dwarf orbiting a Sun-like star, rather than a red dwarf. Researchers noted the signal’s 8-minute pulsation period differs from earlier long-period transients, which had periods of 18 and 21 minutes. The team analyzed 100 hours of data, confirming the white dwarf’s orbital motion and detecting stellar flares on its companion star. Follow-up observations with the Keck Observatory validated the G-type star’s presence, suggesting future detections could help locate hidden white dwarfs. 'This is the first time the pulses are clear enough to see the white dwarf moving in its orbit,' said lead author Sam McSweeney. The discovery expands understanding of long-period transients and their origins.

item.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Resigns Amid Scandal Over Multiple Affairs
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica, The Verge, TechCrunch, Engadget, Gizmodo
Nvidia founder and former CEO Jensen Huang resigned after multiple extramarital affairs were revealed, including a relationship with an alleged Chinese spy and a senior executive. His departure triggered a 10% drop in Nvidia’s stock, erasing over $400 billion in market value. Federal investigations are underway into the alleged spy connection, while the company faces scrutiny over its ties to China amid U.S. export controls. CFO Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent successor. Huang’s resignation ends his three-decade leadership, during which Nvidia became central to AI infrastructure. The board cited national security concerns and a need for stability, appointing Kress, who joined Nvidia in 2013. Legal actions, including a class-action lawsuit, have been launched. Mixed reactions from the tech community highlight the controversy, with some supporting Huang and others criticizing the board’s response. The company’s future in the AI industry remains uncertain amid the fallout.
item.source: Ars Technica, The Verge, TechCrunch, Engadget, Gizmodo

item.title: Hackers exploit AntiFox AI tool to steal AWS credentials
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: AntiFox AI agents hijacked by hackers to carry out theft of AWS credentials
Cybercriminals are exploiting the open-source AI-powered pentesting tool AntiFox to steal Amazon Web Services (AWS) credentials. Security researchers at Arctic Wolf reported that threat actors host AntiFox instances on Alibaba Cloud, using its automated features to analyze compromised systems, search for passwords, and access cloud resources. Attackers first compromise internet-facing Microsoft IIS servers, install web shells, and extract database credentials to access internal production databases or AWS accounts. Amazon confirmed its services were not compromised but urged customers to secure credentials and follow best practices. AntiFox, a fork of the Chinese-developed ARTEX framework, has been linked to recent cyberattacks, including breaches of South Korean financial institutions. Researchers advise monitoring web servers for suspicious activity, rotating exposed credentials, and restricting application permissions. ARTEX, released in late 2026, saw rapid adoption but was later closed-source after being used in attacks. Arctic Wolf recommends immediate action to detect and mitigate unauthorized access.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: INSTRUCTION: AI surgical edit prompts reduce unintended text changes
item.description:
Source: PCWorld Original headline: ChatGPT’s edits going too far? This prompt keeps them surgical
Users can direct AI models like ChatGPT, Claude Opus 5.5, and Gemini Argon to make precise edits without altering other text using a 'surgical edit' prompt. The prompt instructs the AI to modify only specified parts while preserving the rest of the document. Testing showed models without the prompt made numerous unwanted changes, such as replacing casual language with formal phrasing or removing hedges. With the surgical prompt, collateral edits dropped significantly. The longer version of the prompt also lists all changes made, aiding review. In tests, ChatGPT still made minor edits even with the prompt, while Gemini Argon and Claude Opus 5.5 avoided unauthorized changes. The full prompt is more likely to ask users to define filler words, ensuring clarity.

item.title: Major Companies Report Minimal AI Agent Usage in Services
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News, Gizmodo Original headline: AI Agents Face Low Adoption as Major Companies Report Minimal Usage
Uber, DoorDash, and Airbnb reported minimal AI agent usage. Uber disclosed four AI bookings versus 320 million human-driven trips during Halloween week. DoorDash CEO Tony Xu noted AI agents handled several hundred orders, a small fraction of daily billions. Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky called AI-generated bookings 'very non-material.' United Airlines blocked AI agents for bookings, citing privacy risks and regulatory hurdles like baggage screening. Alibaba restricted Claude Code use, while Sweden blocked Claude and ChatGPT over security concerns. Industry analysts suggest current processes are efficient enough, with Uber’s CFO stating ride bookings take about 50 seconds. Companies and governments have distanced themselves from AI agents, indicating widespread adoption remains unlikely despite initial optimism about efficiency gains.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News, Gizmodo

item.title: Prehistoric Hunters in Arabia Used Plant Poison for Spears
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: Prehistoric Hunters in Arabia May Have Had a Secret Weapon—Plant Poison
Scientists discovered traces of plant poison on stone tools at Uruq Aljelibah, a 125,000-year-old site in Saudi Arabia. The findings, published in Science, reveal prehistoric humans used sophisticated weapons with poison to hunt animals like hippos, gazelles, and camels. Chris Clarkson, lead author, noted the tools included adhesives and plant fibers, suggesting advanced technology. The site, once a freshwater lake in 'Green Arabia,' supported permanent human settlement, challenging the notion that Paleolithic Arabia had sparse occupation. Frans van Buchem, corresponding author, highlighted the site’s inland location and older age compared to previous finds. Organic residues on tools preserved details of hunting practices, including potential use of arrow poison tree toxins. The study underscores early humans’ technological complexity, with future research focusing on poison preparation methods and other sites near the ancient lake.

item.title: FBI Warns North Korea's FaceStealer Scheme Hijacks Identities, Spreads Malware
item.description:
Source: PCMag Original headline: FBI: North Korea's 'FaceStealer' Scheme Can Hijack Identities, Spread Malware
FBI warns North Korea's FaceStealer scheme hijacks identities and spreads malware. The campaign, linked to state-sponsored group APT 38, has targeted at least 900 people. Federal officials revealed the FBI seized over 900 webcam videos of victims. Hackers use fake LinkedIn, Telegram, and Discord accounts to impersonate trusted contacts, then lure victims into video calls via lookalike domains. During calls, victims are tricked into visiting a link that installs malware, which steals cryptocurrency, passwords, and contact lists. The malware also captures webcam footage for identity theft and AI deepfakes. The FBI estimates the scheme has generated over $400 million in cryptocurrency. Targets include cryptocurrency users and open-source developers, enabling North Korea to tamper with software projects to infect broader audiences. The FBI emphasized the use of multiple fake participants in calls to pressure victims into 'fixing' audio errors.

item.title: GENTO Debuts 21-DoF Dexterous Hand at CoRL 2026
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: GENTO Debuts a 21-DoF Hand at CoRL 2026 as NVIDIA Launches GR00T 2 With TIANJI Marvin Pro
GENTO's 21-degree-of-freedom dexterous hand debuts at CoRL 2026, addressing four mechanical challenges: backlash, fragility, backdrivability, and fingertip force. The hand uses high-precision linkage transmission, impact-resistant design, and MIT hybrid control for compliant interaction. Tianji Intelligence showcases the hand alongside TIANJI Marvin Pro and GR00T 2, NVIDIA's open-world action model. The hardware includes MEMS torque sensors detecting 0.02 N·m with 160 Hz bandwidth and ±0.03 mm accuracy. Benchmark tests show tracking error reduced from 10.56 mm to 1.89 mm. GENTO Luna, a wheeled humanoid platform, demonstrates real-time item handovers. NVIDIA's GR00T 2 uses TIANJI Marvin Pro for skill-transfer tasks like preparing banana yogurt. Tianji Intelligence, incubated by Yaskawa Electric and Everwin Precision, claims 2,000 force-controlled arms deployed in 2025 and 45 global partners. The exhibition runs until 1:00 p.m. on November 11 at Booth 602.

item.title: "Hey Google" has had a good run, but "Hey Gemini" is officially here
item.description:
Source: Latest from Android Central
Google has launched its first Android XR smart glasses, introducing the 'Hey Gemini' hotword for activating its AI assistant. The new glasses replace the previous 'Hey Google' command, marking a shift toward Gemini as the primary AI interface. While the 'Hey Gemini' phrase is now available on the smart glasses, existing Android phones and smart home devices still use 'Hey Google.' The change signals Google's broader integration of Gemini into its services, including apps like Sheets and Gmail. The company has been phasing out Google Assistant since last year, gradually replacing it with Gemini. Google hasn't confirmed when other devices will adopt the new hotword, but the move underscores its focus on Gemini as the central AI experience. The launch highlights the evolving interaction methods for AI assistants, with the new command representing a clear departure from previous branding.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Adobe Acrobat 2026 Guide: Edit PDFs with Free and Paid Tools
item.description:
Source: PCMag Original headline: How to Edit a PDF in 2026 Using Adobe Acrobat
Adobe Acrobat 2026 allows users to edit PDFs using free and paid tools. Basic editing, like text and image changes, is available in the free Acrobat Reader app and online tools, while advanced features such as page reordering, OCR for scanned documents, and AI-powered editing require subscriptions. Acrobat Standard ($14.99/month) enables text/image edits, page management, and form filling. Acrobat Pro ($19.99/month) adds OCR, file comparison, and redaction. AI Assistant Plus, available with Studio ($24.99/month) or as a standalone add-on, lets users describe text changes via natural language and stylize PDFs. Free online tools offer limited edits, one transaction every 30 days. Mobile users can edit PDFs with Acrobat Standard/Pro on iOS/Android. Scanned PDFs can be edited via OCR in Pro. The AI Assistant Plus, launched in August 2026, enhances document customization and workflow efficiency. Commercial and team use require paid plans. Free tools suffice for occasional form filling, while paid subscriptions unlock full editing capabilities.

item.title: Apex Compute Launches DLSS Alternative With Wider GPU Support
item.description:
Source: PCMag Original headline: Apex Compute Shows Off Its DLSS Alternative, And It Works on AMD Cards
Apex Compute has launched a competitor to Nvidia's DLSS called Apex Neural Rendering (ANR), claiming it offers faster performance, lower GPU resource usage, and better visual quality. The technology includes super-resolution upscaling, ray reconstruction denoising, and frame generation, with a demo showcasing improved artifact reduction and smoother object edges. Apex claims its algorithm has lower latency, 1.01ms per frame at 2X compared to DLSS's 1.26ms. It also uses less memory, requiring 214MB for 4K rendering versus DLSS's 562MB. ANR supports a broader range of GPUs, including AMD's RX 5000 series and newer, RTX 20-series, GTX 16-series, Intel Arc A- and B-series, Steam Deck, and Apple silicon. Compatibility extends to Windows 10/11, Linux, and SteamOS with Proton. While ray reconstruction and full upscaling are still in development, the frame-generation demo highlights its potential as an alternative to Nvidia's and AMD's existing upscaling solutions.

item.title: Fireworks AI Breach Exposes Notion Customers' Chat Data
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Cyberattack on Fireworks AI allowed hackers to access Notion customers’ chat transcripts
Fireworks AI confirmed a cyberattack that allowed hackers to access customer data, including Notion's chat transcripts. The breach occurred when attackers breached Fireworks' cloud provider, gaining access to its development system and stealing billing information and datasets. Notion disclosed the breach affected about 1% of its customers, with hackers obtaining chat transcripts from Notion AI users of the 'Insights' feature. The data includes inputs and outputs from AI models but is largely unattributable. Notion disconnected from Fireworks, deleted stored data, and halted connectivity after being notified of the incident. Fireworks attributed the breach to financially motivated hackers targeting large language models (LLMs) to sell tokens. This marks the second breach at Fireworks in two months, following a security incident in October. The incident highlights risks of relying on third-party tech providers for data security.

item.title: AI Demand Drives PCB Supply Shortages, Lead Times Hit 30 Months
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: First RAM, now circuit boards: AI demand is stretching some PCB orders to 30 months
AI demand is driving PCB supply shortages, with lead times reaching 30 months. HP and Dell struggle to secure circuit boards as AI server boards require more layers and materials, consuming more factory time. PCB manufacturers prioritize higher-margin AI work, leaving PC makers in a difficult position. Unimicron chairman S.C. Chien reported 30-month lead times for key equipment, with over 80% of production facing delays. One laminate supplier has orders filling through 2030 despite planned capacity tripling by 2028. Nittobo controls 90% of T-glass for advanced substrates, with expansion taking years. While major OEMs with long-term contracts may weather price rises, smaller brands face potential price hikes or reduced specs in 2027. A Broadcom director noted PCB lead times increased from six weeks to six months, while ILFA reported standard FR-4 laminate lead times extending to four weeks. Suppliers benefit from scarcity narratives, though upstream bottlenecks remain real.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: FAA Deploys AI Tool to Manage National Airspace Traffic
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica, Gizmodo Original headline: FAA Expands AI Tool to Manage National Airspace Traffic
The FAA has expanded its $875 million SMART system to manage U.S. airspace nationwide. Initially tested in Washington, D.C. airspace since September 21, the AI tool rerouted 180 flights, saving an average of 10 minutes per flight and 80 gallons of fuel. The agency plans to deploy SMART across all 22 regional air traffic control centers to reduce delays, lower fuel use, and improve efficiency. The system integrates weather, flight path, traffic flow, and staffing data to predict patterns and recommend routes, though FAA specialists validate recommendations before controllers act. Human controllers retain final authority over SMART’s suggestions. While airline executives support the rollout, the National Air Traffic Controllers Association (NATCA) raised concerns about its design and workforce impact. Democrats in the House sent a letter to the GAO to review safety risks and lack of controller input during development. The Trump administration promoted SMART as a solution to air traffic inefficiencies, with former Secretary Sean Duffy endorsing it. Airlines eased concerns after FAA officials confirmed a 90-day test period before full deployment. The FAA aims to replicate the D.C. success across the national airspace system.

item.title: Lego’s BrickLink marketplace remains offline after unusual activity
item.description:
Source: The Verge Original headline: Lego’s BrickLink marketplace has been offline for a week following ‘unusual activity’
Lego’s BrickLink marketplace has been offline since November 5th due to 'unusual activity.' The company took the site offline to secure the platform, protect users, and ensure data integrity, but has not provided a return date. A statement from Lego notes the team is investigating the incident and addressing related issues before restoring the site. This follows a similar outage in 2020 caused by a cybersecurity incident involving a ransom demand. Lego previously shut down BrickLink 'out of an abundance of caution' and required users to change passwords upon recovery, though accounts were not compromised. The current situation lacks specific details on the cause or timeline for restoration.

item.title: Archaeologists Discover 2,300-Year-Old Tomb of Demeter Priestess in Italy
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: Archaeologists Uncovered a 2,300-Year-Old Tomb in Italy. It May Have Belonged to an Ancient Cult Priestess
Archaeologists discovered a 2,300-year-old tomb in Manduria, Italy, believed to belong to a priestess of the Greek goddess Demeter. The tomb, dated to the 4th–3rd century BCE, was found within the ruins of the ancient Messapian city, which was home to the Iapygian tribe. Inscriptions in the Messapian language and Greek-style decorations, including a thymiaterion for incense burning, suggest the site was linked to the Demeter cult. The tomb, labeled 'Tomb 17,' was part of a group of 23 nearby graves, offering insights into ancient Manduria's religious and urban practices. Researchers, including Stefania Montanaro and Vincenzo Ria, noted the find complicates historical narratives of Greek-Iapygian tensions, as the cult of Demeter predates known conflicts. The site, located near the ancient Greek colony of Tarentum, will undergo conservation and may be displayed at the Archaeological Museum of Manduria. The discovery was announced at a press conference on October 29, 2026, highlighting its significance for understanding ancient religious practices and cultural exchange.

item.title: ACS Recommends Routine PSA Testing for Most Men Starting at 50
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica, Gizmodo Original headline: American Cancer Society Updates Prostate Cancer Screening Guidelines to Include Routine PSA Testing
The American Cancer Society updated prostate cancer screening guidelines to recommend routine PSA blood tests for most men starting at age 50. Men at average risk should undergo testing every two years from 50 to 69. Higher-risk groups, including Black men and those with family history, should begin testing earlier: Black men at 45 annually, and non-Black men with a close relative diagnosed before 65 or multiple relatives at 45. Those with one relative diagnosed at 65 or older may start testing every two years at 45. Men 70-74 should consult doctors about continuing screening, while those 75 and older are generally discouraged from testing. The guidelines highlight PSA testing’s role in detecting aggressive cancers early, citing studies showing reduced mortality and distant-stage disease. Advances in diagnostics now allow less invasive management of slow-growing tumors. This contrasts with 2010 guidelines emphasizing shared decision-making. The ACS notes prostate cancer is the second leading cause of cancer death in men, with 36,000 annual deaths, but warns against overtesting in older men. The US Preventive Services Task Force is updating its own recommendations, with recent changes including new members with potential conflicts of interest.

item.title: Slow Laptop Performance Could Be Battery-Related
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: Your slow laptop might just have a battery problem
Laptop performance issues may stem from battery management settings or hardware. When unplugged, laptops throttle CPU and GPU performance to conserve battery life, leading to slower speeds. Gaming laptops often prioritize plugged-in use due to significant performance drops on battery. Windows 11's 'Best power efficiency' mode prioritizes battery life over speed, while 'Energy Saver' limits background activity when battery levels drop. A failing battery can also cause performance problems even when plugged in, as some systems use battery power to supplement charging during heavy workloads. Dell's Hybrid Power technology exemplifies this. Users should check battery health via Windows' built-in tool by running 'powercfg /batteryreport' to assess capacity loss. Faulty chargers or underpowered adapters may also contribute to performance issues. If performance drops persist after checking settings and battery health, contacting the manufacturer under warranty is recommended.

item.title: Stela lets macOS run on x86-64 PCs via Apple Silicon translation
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: macOS on PC becomes possible again thanks to Apple Silicon translator for x86-64
Apple's shift to Arm-based chips ended Intel Mac compatibility, but Tyler Smith's Stela project now allows macOS to run on x86-64 PCs. Stela, a Linux-based UEFI tool, translates AArch64 instructions to x86-64 using ahead-of-time and JIT compilation, presenting a virtual M2 Mac Mini to macOS. Users boot via USB with a macOS image, requiring 8 GB RAM, UEFI, GPT, and an Nvidia GPU from 16xx to 5000 series. Ethernet support is extensive, but Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and some hardware are limited. The project, in early development, warns of instability and slowness, though it's gaining traction. Smith aims for full Linux kernel hardware support. Pre-translating macOS for x86-64 faces challenges, including code not existing in disk images. Despite limitations, Stela enables running macOS on non-Apple hardware without modifying the OS image.

item.title: Hugging Face CEO Promises to Continue Open Source AI Fight After Huang's Exit
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Hugging Face CEO vows to keep fighting for open source AI after Jensen Huang’s exit
Hugging Face CEO Clément Delangue expressed sadness over Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s departure, calling it a 'really sad day.' Huang’s exit follows Nvidia’s $12.9 billion acquisition of Hugging Face, the second-largest deal in the company’s history. Delangue vowed to 'keep fighting for open-source AI, harder than ever' on X, addressing concerns about Nvidia’s future stance on open-source after Huang’s departure. The U.S. Department of Justice is reviewing the deal’s impact on AI market competition. Huang, a long-time advocate for open-source and open-weight AI, had pushed for policies to prevent over-restriction of such models, emphasizing their role in accessibility and innovation. His advocacy extended to a 2025 policy letter signed by 25 companies, including Microsoft and Meta, urging the U.S. government to support open models. Nvidia also announced a $6 billion partnership with Poolside to build an open AI ecosystem and expanded its Nemotron models. The Hugging Face deal remains on track to close in early 2027.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: How to choose the right mattress for side sleepers
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends
Side sleepers require a mattress that balances cushioning for shoulders and hips with sufficient support to maintain spinal alignment. Key factors include pressure relief, firmness, materials like memory foam or hybrids, and motion isolation for shared beds. Memory foam contours closely, while hybrids combine foam with coils for responsiveness. Firmness preferences vary by weight and movement habits, with medium or medium-soft options often recommended. Adjustable firmness allows customization, and trial periods with warranties help assess suitability. The Sleep Number ComfortNext Ultra offers adjustable firmness via its Tri-Brid design and Responsive Air technology, with independent settings for couples. It includes cooling features and sleep tracking via an app, starting at $4,499. Mattresses that are too firm or too soft can cause discomfort, so testing over multiple nights is advised. Shared-bed comfort depends on motion isolation and individual firmness preferences, which can be addressed with independent controls.

item.title: Volunteers Seek Autonomy, Fewer NDAs in Brain Implant Trials
item.description:
Source: MIT Technology Review Original headline: More autonomy, fewer NDAs: Volunteers have new requests for brain implant trials
Scientists and volunteers are pushing for new ethical guidelines for brain-computer interface (BCI) trials. Ian Burkhart, who had a brain implant since 2014, co-founded the BCI Pioneers Coalition to advocate for participants' rights. The guidelines, published Tuesday, emphasize recognizing volunteers' contributions, compensating them for time and effort, and allowing access to their own brain data. They also call for reducing reliance on nondisclosure agreements (NDAs) and ensuring participants can share data with doctors. Privacy concerns include managing brain data and preparing participants for media attention. The guidelines address post-trial care, urging researchers to maintain devices for a 'reasonable period' and fund removal surgeries. Rita Leggett’s experience, where her implant was removed against her will after a company went bankrupt, highlights the need for ethical post-trial support. While some guidelines overlap with existing standards, the group aims to refine them over time. Jennifer Chandler, a neuroethics professor, called the document 'version one' of an evolving framework.

item.title: Dutch Company's Fiber-Optic Tech Attracts Global Naval Interest
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: Navies queue up for billion-dollar European miltech company which humbles fiber-optic
Dutch defense tech company Optics11 is developing fiber-optic sensors for underwater surveillance, attracting interest from multiple navies. Its systems detect acoustic disturbances using light through optical fibers, identifying oil tankers from 100 kilometers away. CEO Paul Heiden said the technology offers superior acoustic data compared to conventional sonar, requiring proprietary software to process dense datasets. Third-party software couldn't handle the data, prompting Optics11 to develop its own AI-driven solutions, reducing software developers from 60-80 to 10. The company works with Saab, Thales, and Ocean Infinity, among others, and is developing a towed sensor for the Royal Netherlands Navy's Orka-class submarines. Optics11 raised €100 million in 15 months, including €25 million from the European Investment Bank, and plans a 2027 funding round targeting a $1 billion valuation. It aims for positive cash flow by 2028 and expansion into Southeast Asia and the Middle East. The firm keeps sensitive developments confidential, citing risks of exposing military capabilities. Heiden emphasized Dutch government support for maintaining secrecy.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: Whoop Launches Social Network for Fitness Data Sharing
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch, Engadget
Whoop, a fitness tracker company, launched a social network called Whoop Humans within its app for all members at no cost. The platform enables users to follow friends and family, share health data like sleep, recovery, workouts, and achievements, and interact via comments and reactions. Unlike Teams, a group-based leaderboard feature, Whoop Humans focuses on personalized connections with privacy controls. CEO Will Ahmed stated the network is opt-in, with options to hide activity in 'stealth mode' and restrict sensitive metrics. Health alerts and medical data are not shared by default, and users can report inappropriate content. A 'Moments' feature allows sharing workout photos with privacy settings. Data on the network comes exclusively from Whoop's wearables, addressing concerns about artificial content. The company noted 'huge growth' among users over 60, partly due to medical wellness expansion, including FDA-cleared ECG and blood pressure insights. Whoop is part of a Medicare program reimbursing wearables with health benefits. Ahmed highlighted that low recovery scores engage users more than perfect metrics. The platform could also serve family monitoring, like adult children checking on aging parents. Whoop clarified it does not sell or license member data, positioning itself as a 'membership' product. The launch aligns with industry trends toward consolidation in wearable and health tech, with Ahmed noting expectations for more mergers among AI, clinician-focused, and wearable companies.

item.title: Exoplanet TOI-2535b Disappears from Observations
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: The amazing disappearing exoplanet
Exoplanet TOI-2535b, a hot Jupiter-sized planet orbiting star TOI-2535, has stopped showing up in observations after seven years of regular transits. Researchers suspect an unseen companion planet in a different orbital plane is causing the disappearance. TOI-2535, a K dwarf star, was identified by TESS as hosting a Jupiter-sized planet with an eight-day orbit. Analysis of transit timing revealed shifts up to six hours, suggesting gravitational interactions with an undetected planet. The companion’s orbit, likely tilted relative to the system’s plane, prevents it from passing between the star and Earth, explaining why it remains hidden. The finding highlights challenges in detecting exoplanets with misaligned orbits, as the unseen planet’s influence alters transit timing without direct detection.

item.title: Halo Campaign Evolved Gets Free Firefight Mode Update
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Halo: Campaign Evolved finally gets the replay value fans asked for
Xbox CEO Asha Sharma confirmed Halo: Campaign Evolved will receive a free Firefight mode update this winter. The addition includes new maps, weapons, and four-player co-op, offering wave-based combat with escalating difficulty. Fans previewed the mode at Xbox FanFest on November 12, with more details set for Halo Fest December 12-13. The update addresses the remake's lack of replay value, providing varied gameplay through modifiers and cooperative play. It marks part of Xbox's 25th anniversary celebrations, aligning with Halo's status as the original Xbox's launch title. Firefight's free access and dynamic challenges aim to extend the game's longevity beyond the main campaign.

item.title: Norwest Launches $4B AI Fund to Expand Tech Investments
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Norwest pushes deeper into AI with new $4B fund
Norwest, backed by Wells Fargo, has raised a $4 billion fund as part of its 18th investment vehicle and largest to date. The fund targets AI startups across sectors like consumer, healthcare, and technology, with investments in the U.S., India, and Israel. Jeff Crowe, senior managing partner, emphasized a broad AI strategy, stating, 'We’re taking a broad approach to AI because its impact is broad.' The firm focuses on AI-native applications, physical AI, domain-specific models, and cybersecurity. Recent investments include Coval, which develops AI agent testing tools, and Generalist AI, a robotics foundation model startup. Since closing its $3 billion 17th fund in 2024, Norwest has made over 87 investments. Crowe highlighted AI's potential to transform enterprise, consumer, and healthcare solutions across multiple industries.

item.title: Phota Labs uses AI to enhance photos without altering authenticity
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Phota Labs uses AI to turn everyday photos into professional-looking shots
Phota Labs, an iOS app backed by a16z, uses AI to transform everyday photos into professional-looking images while preserving authenticity. Founded by Cecilia Zhang and Zach Xia, former Adobe employees, the app addresses gaps in existing editing tools by focusing on improving poorly captured photos rather than just enhancing them. Zhang described Phota as a "personal photo assistant" that proactively enhances images, akin to a virtual photographer. The app offers customizable styles, from subtle edits to dramatic transformations, and employs personalization tech to maintain user identity in AI-generated images. Watermarks identify AI-altered photos on social platforms. Targeting users who take many photos for social media, Phota aims to expand to retirees and parents. Xia emphasized authenticity, stating the app ensures photos remain real moments rather than AI-generated images. The startup raised $5.6 million in seed funding and plans to launch a free app before exploring a freemium model, with an Android version in the future.

item.title: Microsoft releases 25 original Xbox games on PC for anniversary
item.description:
Source: The Verge Original headline: Here are the 25 original Xbox games you can now play on PC
Microsoft is making 25 original Xbox games available on PC for its 25th anniversary. These games require digital purchases and are playable with keyboard and mouse. Achievements are being added to four titles: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, Blinx: The Time Sweeper, and Conker: Live and Reloaded, with updates coming to Xbox One and Series consoles. The full list includes 21 new additions, such as multiple Star Wars titles, though many already have PC versions. Original Xbox discs cannot be used due to the absence of Microsoft’s serial number system. Xbox on PC backward compatibility uses an emulator. Most new games aren’t part of Xbox Game Pass, except Blinx, Conker, Crimson Skies, Fusion Frenzy, Morrowind, and Grabbed by the Ghoulies. Leaked documents indicated a 2026 full launch for original Xbox games on PC, with Xbox 360 games rolling out to next-gen consoles between 2027 and 2028. The Xbox Helix, expected as a Windows PC, will support games from all Xbox generations.

item.title: Former BioWare Exec's Free RPG Offers Console-Quality Mobile Experience
item.description:
Source: Latest from Android Central Original headline: This free RPG from a former BioWare exec's studio promises a console-quality experience — all on your phone
A new free-to-play mobile RPG, UnGodly, launched on Google Play. Developed by Azra Games, founded by former BioWare and EA executive Mark Otero, the game is a dark fantasy action RPG following mercenary Vander and his squad of divine warriors called Primals. Each Primal, descended from an ancient god, offers unique combat abilities, with over 20 unlockable characters including Conan the Barbarian via a crossover. Character progression features quests and relationships, with gameplay designed for short sessions. Otero claims the game delivers 'console-quality depth, fidelity, and experience' comparable to PC or console titles. Available now on Google Play with PC controls via Google Play Games, it will expand to Samsung Galaxy Store and One Store next month. The game promises tens of hours of play with meaningful progression per session.

item.title: Microsoft Outlook Still Down as Recovery Efforts Continue
item.description:
Source: The Verge, Latest from Android Central, Digital Trends Original headline: Microsoft Outlook Outage Continues as Recovery Efforts Underway
Microsoft Outlook remains offline globally, disrupting email and Microsoft 365 services like SharePoint Online and Teams. The outage, which began on November 12, has affected hundreds of thousands of users across web, desktop, and mobile platforms. Microsoft initially cited elevated regional loads as the cause but later identified unexpected server unavailability overwhelming infrastructure. Affected servers failed automated health checks, though no recent change was linked to the outage’s start. Engineers are addressing server-side issues, extending email timeouts to 48 hours, restarting servers, rerouting traffic, and testing alternative health-check methods. Some servers have stabilized, but full capacity is not yet restored. Microsoft reports improvements in mailbox access and email processing, but intermittent issues persist. Teams and SharePoint Online are also impacted, with incident IDs EX1550543 and MO1550821. Users are advised to monitor the Microsoft 365 status page for updates as recovery continues.
item.source: The Verge, Latest from Android Central, Digital Trends

item.title: Leaders Acknowledge AI's Workplace Importance, But Implementation Lags
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: Leaders agree AI is vital for their workplace — but barely any are doing anything about it
A Lenovo report reveals that 80% of IT leaders recognize AI's potential for the workplace, but only 10% have implemented digital transformations to support it. The sixth volume of the Lenovo Work Reborn report, based on a 1,200-person survey across nine countries, highlights a growing 'AI readiness divide.' While AI is being scaled across business functions, just 10% of organizations have rethought work processes for AI integration. Similarly, only 10% have governance frameworks for AI tools and data access. Fewer than 10% measure AI's return on investment, with many adopting a 'fire and forget' approach. The AI Workplace Readiness Index scores range from 2.7 for organizations evaluating AI to 4.1 for those fully utilizing it. Rakshit Ghura, Lenovo's Vice President, emphasizes the need for measurable value from AI, such as reduced cycle times and improved outcomes. He argues that outdated workplaces hinder AI effectiveness, stressing the importance of redesigning workflows and governance for AI integration.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: West Virginia online casinos hit October revenue record
item.description:
Source: ReadWrite Original headline: West Virginia online casinos set October record in bet365’s second full month
West Virginia online casinos recorded $37,198,210 in adjusted gross interactive wagering receipts in October 2026, the second full month bet365 operated in the state. This surpassed the total revenue of all of 2025. The revenue, defined as gross receipts minus player winnings, funds the Interactive Wagering Fund. Bet365, which launched online sports betting and casino in West Virginia on August 27, 2026, is its fourth U.S. market. The state’s capped market allows no more than five gaming licenses, with online games treated as state-owned lottery games. A pending tax bill, House Bill 4397, would raise the iGaming privilege tax. The Lottery reported $1.33 billion in gross revenue for fiscal 2026, up $58 million from 2025, with iGaming as a key growth area. The next report will detail operator contributions, including bet365’s share of October’s record.

item.title: Old power banks should not be tossed in trash; proper disposal methods and safety tips outlined
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: Don't toss that old power bank in the trash — here's where it actually goes
Old power banks should not be tossed in trash; proper disposal methods and safety tips outlined. Lithium-ion batteries in power banks are flammable and require careful disposal. Users should check local laws and find designated recycling centers or drop-off points. Hardware stores like Lowe's and Home Depot partner with organizations such as The Battery Network for safe disposal. Power banks showing swelling, overheating, or charge retention loss should be discarded immediately due to explosion risks. Certifications like CCC, FCC, and UL 2056 indicate safety compliance, while 'TSA-approved' claims lack official verification. Consumers are advised to purchase certified products and avoid uncertified models for safety.

item.title: SATA SSDs' Era Ends as PCIe and NVMe Surpass Speed Limits
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: How the SATA SSD era ended in failure, and why nobody should miss it
SATA SSDs' era ends as PCIe and NVMe surpass speed limits. SATA, introduced in 2009, was designed for hard drives, not SSDs, and its 600MB/s cap is now exceeded by high-end HDDs. SATA SSDs quickly saturated bandwidth, limiting performance gains despite advancements. Modern PCIe-based SSDs like Samsung's 970 EVO Plus (3.5GB/s) outpace SATA III drives by over six times. M.2 form factors using NVMe offer four PCIe lanes, enabling faster data access and compact designs. While SATA SSDs remain relevant for basic storage tasks, their performance limitations make them obsolete for demanding applications. Techspot tests showed minimal performance differences between NVMe and SATA SSDs in gaming, but video editors and data-heavy workflows benefit from faster drives. SATA SSDs are still usable for everyday tasks and cost-effective in current markets, but their long-term relevance is declining as PCIe 5.0 and newer technologies advance.

item.title: Mass Effect Composer Warns AI Can’t Replace Human Creativity in Games
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: ‘AI is not an artist’ — Mass Effect 1 and 2 composer shares his stance on AI replacement in video games, says ‘Machines can never be artists as they aren’t human’
Mass Effect and Mass Effect 2 composer Jack Wall criticized AI's role in video games, arguing it cannot replace human creativity. In an interview with TechRadar Gaming, Wall stated AI should remain a 'creative tool' but warned against replacing human artists. 'Machines can never be artists as they aren’t human,' he said, emphasizing that art's purpose is human communication. Wall dismissed AI music as mere replication of existing work, stressing that creative decisions must remain human. Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 composer Jason Graves echoed similar concerns, calling AI incapable of replicating human emotional depth and inspiration. As AI adoption grows in gaming, composers warn against its overuse, highlighting the irreplaceable value of human artistry in creating emotionally resonant experiences. Studios and tech firms like Nvidia have increasingly integrated AI tools, sparking debate over their impact on creative processes.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: Elder Scrolls Mobile Game Gets 4K PC Port
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: The Elder Scrolls' most obscure adventure gets a 4K PC makeover
A fan-made PC port of The Elder Scrolls Travels: Shadowkey, a 2004 mobile game, now offers a 4K experience. The free project, titled Shadowkey: Reforged, updates the original game's graphics, art, and interface while retaining its core mechanics. The original game, released for Nokia N-Gage devices, featured 176 x 208 resolution and 25 fps gameplay. The new version scales to 16:9 monitors with up to 120 fps, includes retextured models, bloom lighting, rippling water, and sharper text rendering. The port runs natively on PC without requiring emulators or vintage hardware. Developers note the game's internal logic remains tied to its original 25 fps frame rate. The project fills a gap for long-time fans who missed the mobile release, offering a modernized version of the obscure title.

item.title: Noctua launches space-grade carbon nanotube thermal pad for AMD processors
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Noctua brings space-grade carbon nanotube thermal pad to AMD AM5 and AM4 processors
Noctua has launched its NT-CP1 thermal pad for AMD AM4 and AM5 processors, utilizing Carbice's carbon nanotube technology originally developed for aerospace applications. The $24.95 pad features vertically-aligned carbon nanotubes that conform to CPU surfaces over time, improving heat transfer performance during initial use and maintaining stability for years. Unlike conventional thermal pastes, the NT-CP1 uses an aluminum core with a nanoscale polymer coating for durability and electrical insulation. It offers a simple peel-and-press installation and fits both AM4 and AM5 sockets. Noctua claims the manufacturing process uses recycled aluminum and waste carbon gas, making it more energy-efficient than traditional graphite-based pads. CEO Roland Mossig highlighted the product's ease of use and long-term reliability, noting its maintenance-free design and recyclability through standard aluminum channels.

item.title: Adobe Executives Warn Marketing Orgs Must Adapt to AI-Driven Changes
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: 'You cannot change or build the marketing organization of the future with the creative organization of the past': Adobe CEO lays out how work and collaboration are fundamentally changing
Adobe executives warn marketing organizations must evolve beyond outdated structures to keep pace with AI-driven changes. CEO Shantanu Narayen and Creative VP Resh Sidhu emphasized that marketing teams face unprecedented pressure to create content across multiple languages and geographies while adapting to faster refresh cycles. Sidhu argued that entire organizational frameworks must be reimagined, stating, 'You cannot change or build the marketing organization of the future with the creative organization of the past.' The discussion centered on AI's role in transforming workflows, with executives noting that AI is no longer just a tool but a digital colleague reshaping how teams collaborate. Product Marketing VP Deepa Subramaniam and Sidhu highlighted the need for AI literacy, stressing that tracking AI usage frequency is insufficient. They noted AI enables employees to focus on creative development and campaign refinement, but also complicates inter-team responsibilities. While individual creators retain control over AI use, business leaders must redefine work structures as AI democratizes processes. The executives concluded that companies adapting to these changes will thrive, while those resisting risk obsolescence.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: Maersk Confirms Data Breach, Hackers Demand $5M Ransom
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: Shipping giant Maersk confirms data breach as hackers demand $5 million ransom
Maersk confirmed a cyberattack targeting a legacy system from its acquired logistics company LF Logistics. Hackers, claiming to have stolen 100GB of data including driver records, passwords, and mobile device logs, demanded $5 million in bitcoin to prevent leaks. The company stated core operations remain unaffected and found no evidence of data exposure beyond the isolated system. WhiteArmor, the ransomware group, threatened to release the data if payment isn’t made within 30 days. LF Logistics, a Hong Kong-based third-party logistics firm, was acquired by Maersk in 2022 for $3.6 billion. The breach follows a 2017 NotPetya attack that cost Maersk $250–$300 million. Maersk warned that plaintext passwords and admin accounts could compromise its IT security, urging immediate action to secure systems.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: Samsung to Enhance Health App with AI and Hospital Partnerships
item.description:
Source: Latest from Android Central Original headline: Samsung's Health app isn't personal enough—exec weighs in on upcoming changes
Samsung's Health app will undergo major AI-driven changes to offer personalized health insights and better integrate with medical institutions. Digital health vice president Choi Jun-il revealed plans to transform the app into a service by analyzing user data like sleep, exercise, and diet. The company aims to collaborate with South Korean hospitals, sharing wearable sensor data under agreements. Samsung also plans to leverage its U.S. acquisition of Xealth to connect users with over 100 hospitals by 2030, bridging the gap between patient data and doctors. Existing features include virtual doctor visits via HealthTap, Health Records with Walgreens, and a revamped Health app update that tracks daily energy and heart health. While challenges remain, the goal is to standardize health data and provide doctors with direct access to user insights, improving care through AI and partnerships.

item.title: Muse AI now lets paid users place calls to U.S. businesses
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Muse can now place calls to US businesses — if you pay
Meta's Muse AI agent now allows paid subscribers to place calls to U.S. businesses. The feature, tested since September, enables users to handle tasks like contacting cable companies or restaurants. Chief AI officer Alexandr Wang noted the tool could manage calls people avoid. Paid plans start at $20 monthly for 500 million tokens, with higher tiers at $100 monthly. While competitors like Instinct and Gemini offer similar services, many businesses hang up on AI calls. Improved voice mimicry may make detection harder. The feature addresses frustrations with poor customer service, offering AI-driven patience for tedious tasks. Email access will soon be free for all users, though calling remains a paid feature.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Spotify Wrapped 2026: Tips to Customize Your Year-End Summary
item.description:
Source: Latest from Android Central Original headline: Spotify Wrapped is almost here — here are 3 ways to get the perfect end of year summary
Spotify Wrapped is approaching, with the cutoff for final listening hours likely in late November or early December. Users have 2-3 weeks to prepare. The Taste Profile feature allows Premium subscribers in the US and New Zealand to review and adjust how Spotify understands their listening habits, including text prompts for genre or artist recommendations. Blocking artists via the 'Don't play this artist' option removes their music from playlists, Discover Weekly, and Daily Mix. Family plan users can exclude kids' music from Wrapped summaries by enabling a setting that filters family-related content, ensuring it doesn't affect recommendations or Wrapped results.
